title: Purview architecture policy
description: The authoritative project responsibility, naming and dependency policy. The architecture tests read this document. See the purview-architests skill.

$schema.description: Pointer to this schema, so an editor validates the file as it is written.

version.description: Schema version of this document. Increment when a change would break a reader that understood the previous shape. Version 3 adds typeRules, apiRules, portRules, dependencyBudget, policyIntegrity and waiverPolicy; a version-2 document remains valid because all are optional. Version 2 removed the 'rules' object, whose flags were never consulted; use SkipRule, or a waiver, to opt out of a rule.

qualifiedNameSeparator.description: Separates the responsibility from its implementation qualifier, as in Persistence.SqlServer.

dependencyArrowMeaning.description: States what an arrow means, so compile-time references are not confused with runtime calls.

sourceRoots.description: Repo-relative folders holding the projects. Defaults to ["src"]. An empty array scans the repository root, which suits a flat layout. Getting this wrong finds no projects, which the graphDiscovery rule reports rather than passing every other rule vacuously.

responsibilities.description: The responsibility catalogue. A project name is <Responsibility>[.<Implementation>]; only the first segment is classified.

discouragedProjectNames.description: Names that describe a category rather than a responsibility, so nothing can be excluded from them.

assemblyRules.description: The type-level dependency check. It reuses each responsibility's mayDependOn and mustNotDependOn against the types a compiled assembly actually references, so a dependency that only arrives transitively or through a package is caught too.

enabled.description: Whether the type-level check runs. It reads compiled assemblies by metadata only, so it needs a build to have produced them.

assemblyRoots.description: Repo-relative folders to scan for assemblies. An empty array scans the test output directory, which already holds every project the test project references, directly or transitively.

assemblyGlobs.description: File globs matched under each assembly root.

typeRules.description: The type-level naming, shape, namespace and attribute rules. Off by default because they read compiled assemblies and need a build to have produced them.

enabled.description: Whether the type-level rules run. They read the definition tables by metadata only: nothing is loaded or executed.

appliesTo.description: Which responsibilities the rules govern. An empty categories array governs every production responsibility.

excludeGeneratedCode.description: Skip types marked GeneratedCode or CompilerGenerated, so a source generator is not forced to change.

excludeNamespacePrefixes.description: Namespace prefixes whose types are skipped, such as a generated-client namespace.

discouragedTypeSuffixes.description: Type-name suffixes that describe a mechanism rather than a responsibility.

sealConcreteClasses.description: Require a public concrete class to be sealed, unless it is abstract.

requireReadOnlyCollections.description: Reject a public property or method that exposes List<T> or Dictionary<TKey, TValue>; return IReadOnlyList<T> or IReadOnlyDictionary<TKey, TValue> instead.

forbiddenAttributes.description: Attributes no governed public type may carry, by namespace-qualified type name.

requiredAttributes.description: Attributes every governed public type must carry, by namespace-qualified type name.

allowObsoleteWithoutMessage.description: Allow [Obsolete] without a message. Off by default: an obsolete member without a replacement is a dead end.

forbidInternalsVisibleToProduction.description: Report InternalsVisibleTo that names a production assembly. Exposing internals to a test project remains ordinary.

apiRules.description: The committed-API rules. The baseline is the reviewed record of the public surface, so an addition is as deliberate as a removal. Off by default because it needs a build.

baseline.description: The baseline path relative to the repository root.

requireTypeDocumentation.description: Require every public type to have an XML documentation entry. The project must generate its documentation file.

requireMemberDocumentation.description: Require every public member to have an XML documentation entry. Off by default: a record's positional parameters document its properties through the type entry.

portRules.description: The port rules: every interface in a port category has an implementation, and its signature names no infrastructure technology.

categories.description: The categories whose interfaces are treated as ports. Defaults to the inner layers.

forbiddenTypePrefixes.description: Type prefixes a port must not expose, such as a database provider or an HTTP client.

dependencyBudget.description: A ratchet on each project's declared references. The budget records what the graph allows today, so a new dependency needs a reviewed change and a stale allowance is removed.

failOnStale.description: Fail when an allowed reference no longer exists. A stale allowance hides the next dependency.

entries.description: The per-project allowances. A project with no entry is not budgeted; an empty array is a valid starting point.

project.description: The production project name, exactly as it appears on disk.

references.description: The project references the budget permits.

policyIntegrity.description: The policy's own consistency checks. Unknown responsibility names, a dependency that is both permitted and forbidden, and duplicate names or aliases are always reported; reachability is opt-in.

checkReachability.description: Prove each mustNotDependOn is enforceable: a prohibition is meaningless when the permitted mayDependOn closure can reach the forbidden responsibility anyway.

waiverPolicy.description: How long a waiver may go unreviewed. Unset by default, so expiry is opt-in; a policy that adopts it turns reviewedOn from a note into an obligation.

maxAgeDays.description: The maximum age, in days, of a waiver's reviewedOn date. A stale waiver is reported by waiverIntegrity and by 'architests waivers list --stale'.

waivers.description: Deliberate, reviewed departures. A waiver excuses the narrowest thing possible - usually the name - and mapsTo keeps the project classified so every dependency rule still applies.

projectNameSegment.description: A single PascalCase segment, with no dots: the responsibility, not a qualified project name.

aliases.description: Recognised alternative names. An established project using one of these is not renamed.

mayDependOn.description: Responsibilities this one may reference at compile time. An empty array means it depends on nothing.

mustNotDependOn.description: Responsibilities this one must never reference. Must not overlap mayDependOn.

forbiddenPackagePrefixes.description: NuGet identifier prefixes that must not appear in this responsibility, such as Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore in Core.

forbiddenPackageScope.description: What forbiddenPackagePrefixes measures. 'own' checks the packages the project declares or its own package references bring in, excluding packages explained by a permitted project reference; 'closure' checks the whole restore closure, including packages inherited from referenced projects.

forbiddenFrameworkReferences.description: Framework reference prefixes that must not appear in this responsibility, such as Microsoft.AspNetCore.App in a portable layer.

siblingIndependence.description: When true, qualified implementations of this responsibility must not reference one another.

project.description: The project name the waiver applies to, exactly as it appears on disk.

mapsTo.description: The responsibility this project actually has. Keeps every dependency rule in force while excusing the name.

rules.description: The rule ids this waiver excuses. A waiver that excuses nothing does nothing, and an unknown id is reported by the waiverIntegrity rule.

reason.description: Why the departure is acceptable. A blanket suppression with no reason makes the policy unfalsifiable.
